title: A Test Report You Can Read: Scenarios Tied to Hazards, a Table That Names What Is Not Covered, and a Regression It Catches

questions.question: Why is 'all tests pass' not enough to hand to somebody deciding whether to trust the robot?
options: It does not say which hazards were tried: four of the eight had no scenario at all
questions.explanation: The report names G3, G5, G6 and G7.

questions.question: For the link scenario S4, what is the pass?
options: Not reaching it: stopped with cause link and still at the end
questions.explanation: A safety scenario passed by completing the task is not testing safety.

questions.question: The limiter and supervisor are taken out. Which scenarios still pass?
options: The empty building and the doorway: the functional tests pass and the three safety scenarios fail

questions.question: The link scenario is left out of the suite. What does the suite say?
options: Green, and the report lists G2, the unacceptable hazard, as NOT COVERED
questions.explanation: An uncovered hazard is a gap, not a failure of what was tested.

questions.question: Why was the layout of the report tested with results made by hand?
options: So a change to the physics cannot break the report, and a change to the report is one somebody has to look at
questions.explanation: The text is checked to the character.

questions.question: What can the report not tell?
options: Whether a scenario's rule would really catch the hazard, and whether the link between scenario and hazard is true: both are claims a person made
questions.explanation: A covered hazard was tried once, in one building.
